hook.text: In 2013, Snowden revealed the NSA collected phone data on millions of Americans. Legally. With secret courts.

buildup.text: PRISM gave the NSA direct access to Google, Facebook, and Apple servers. Tech companies initially denied it.

discovery.text: Democratic surveillance hides behind national security law. Courts approve it in secret. Oversight is minimal.

twist.text: After Snowden, reforms passed. But the core programs continued. Surveillance shrank in public view, not in practice.

climax.text: Democracies surveil differently than dictatorships—but they still surveil. The tools just wear nicer labels.

punchline.text: Democracies promise freedom. Surveillance agencies collect it.

quiz.question: What did Edward Snowden reveal in 2013?
